briefdescription.para: REST controller for client accounts (users and providers).

detaileddescription.para: This file defines the Clients controller, which manages user and provider accounts. Its endpoints cover account creation, login and logout, suspend/activate, read, update, delete, search and listing a client's services. A {clientType} part of the URL (users or providers) selects one concrete ClientController from a std::variant registry. Create and login are INSECURE (no token needed); the rest are SECURE and use the identity attributes set by Auth. Most handlers either await async controller coroutines or use executeControllerMethod; read also has a prototype asynchronous implementation for users and providers.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: This controller is the HTTP front door for client accounts. Drogon routes the /api/v2 clients URLs here, and its handlers call the shared dispatcher, the GateKeeper, the Validator and a DatabaseController to reach the database. It is the only place that issues and invalidates login tokens (through the login/logout controllers), so it underpins authentication for the whole API. Without it clients could not register, sign in or manage their accounts.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
REST create/read/update/delete (CRUD) routes: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods
Bearer tokens and the Authorization header: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization
HTTP filters/middleware: https://drogon.docsforge.com/master/filter/
C++ coroutines (co_await): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/coroutines
